text:
COMPLETE. All four items done; the earlier partial note is superseded.

1. ssh no longer compile-depends on AGENT. AgentApi moved from agent/AgentService.scala to protocol/AgentApi.scala — it is a wire contract referencing only core and protocol types, and AgentCall/AgentFailure were already there. The ssh conformance suites do drive a real in-process agent, so that edge is now `agent % "test->compile"`: a client may TEST against a server, it may not COMPILE against one.

2. ssh no longer compile-depends on WORKER. The cut is along a seam the code itself revealed: ssh uses exactly operation, inputCodec, outputCodec and retrySafety from a task, and NEVER run. So the submittable half became TaskDefinition[I, O] in a new slurm4s-task module (core + batch only), carrying SlurmTaskCall, SlurmBatch, SlurmBatchOptions and SlurmBatchCompileFailure. ScalaTask now extends TaskDefinition and adds run; SlurmTask extends ScalaTask. A remote client sends an operation and encoded input and reads a typed result back — requiring the executable definition to name that is what forced the client to compile against the worker runtime.

ssh's compile dependencies are now core, batch, task, protocol. Nothing else.

3. Compatibility aliases gone. The worker AtomicFiles facade had no consumers outside its own test; worker production code now imports the kernel object directly, which also removed the fully-qualified workaround C1 had to introduce. SharedKernel.scala already had zero references.

4. KERNEL PURITY — the ADR 0001 fix, and it needed no module split. AtomicFiles' `F[_]: Sync` wrappers were the ONLY Cats Effect reference in the entire kernel, and all 24 uses of them were in tests: every production caller already used the Blocking variants. Removing the wrappers and dropping catsEffect leaves remote-exec-kernel depending on cats-core and scodec-bits alone. Callers wrap with Sync[F].blocking(AtomicFiles.…Blocking(…)), which is where ADR 0001 says the effect belongs.

That resolves the ADR 0001 / ADR 0010 tension without contradicting either: 0010 keeps filesystem mechanics in the kernel, 0001 keeps Cats Effect out of it, because mechanics are blocking calls returning values and effect wrapping is the caller's business.

Coverage note: modules/worker/.../AtomicFilesSuite.scala was emptied rather than rewritten. It existed to test the facade, and its assertions duplicate kernel/AtomicFilesSuite — which now also has AtomicCrossProcessSuite from B3 beside it. No kernel coverage was lost; a duplicate was removed.

Verification: full suite 425 green on Scala 3.3.8 AND 3.8.4, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.

Files emptied and needing git rm: worker/AtomicFiles.scala, worker/Batch.scala, worker/AtomicFilesSuite.scala, core/SharedKernel.scala.
